explanation: Punctuality is formally valued in Thai business culture, and arriving on time is seen as a sign of respect, especially expected of foreign visitors. In practice, Thai meetings often start late, and Thais themselves may run late due to 'kreng jai' — a reluctance to cut off a prior conversation or inconvenience someone else — usually without serious offense or professional consequence. Showing visible frustration about a late start is considered worse manners than the lateness itself.
local_tip: Aim to arrive on time or a few minutes early yourself, but stay relaxed and don't show irritation if your Thai counterparts or the meeting itself runs late.

also_check.note: Punctuality is critical, and even a one-minute delay can be seen as disrespectful.
Arriving 15-30 minutes late to informal plans is common and tolerated, though punctuality is more expected for formal business meetings.
Meetings may start late due to flexible local scheduling, but foreign visitors are still expected to arrive on time.

sources.title: Punctuality in Thailand – Why are Thais Late?
